headline: Predictive models of biomolecular binding extend to force, proteome, and ligand contexts
label: Integrative Biomolecular Conformational Modeling
summary: Predicted structures are now being evaluated against force-spectroscopy observables, proteome-scale export atlases, and ligand-bound RNA benchmarks.
synthesis: The shared thread is computational prediction of biomolecular binding and conformation, extended beyond single static structures toward observables and proteome-scale descriptions. A modified ViennaRNA package models RNA-protein binding under external force and predicts extension changes relevant to single-molecule force spectroscopy. An AlphaFold 3 atlas generates cargo-XPO1-RanGTP complex models for over 4,000 human proteins to map nuclear export sequences at proteome scale. A benchmark of RNA secondary structure predictors on a newly curated ligand-bound RNA dataset is more evaluative in character, reporting accuracy drops for long RNAs and pseudoknots. What is new is the extension of prediction toward force-dependent, ligand-associated, and proteome-wide descriptions of complexes.
